caption: Figure 1. Study workflow: shared anatomical localization and two separate diagnostic tasks.
note: Note. Patient-grouped repeated holdouts and inner out-of-fold predictions separate segmenter fitting from downstream classifier training. The green route assesses predicted masks directly against reference masks; segmentation metrics do not originate from either classifier. Blue and purple routes represent independently fitted binary and direct three-class analyses, respectively, not a diagnostic cascade. Strict predicted-ROI rejection has no manual, reference-mask or full-frame rescue. Raw frame probabilities are aggregated to eyes and then patients before level-specific temperature scaling. Test gates controlled access during execution but did not eliminate prior study-level exposure to the reused holdouts.

caption: Figure 2. Overall held-out anatomical ROI segmentation performance across the four frozen segmenters.
note: Note. Points are five-split means and whiskers sample SD, not confidence intervals. Invalid postprocessed predictions are represented as empty masks: Dice, IoU, and surface Dice receive zero, while area error remains failure-inclusive. Boundary distances require nonempty predictions and must be read with coverage.

caption: Figure 3. Four-model segmentation on identical frames from three held-out patients.
note: Note. Qualitative comparison of postprocessed segmentations in three shared test patients. Rows identify the four models; each column uses an identical frame and reference mask across models. From all 252 frames of the 18 patients in fixed test split seed 17, frames were ranked by the mean Dice across the four models. The maximum, closest-to-median, and minimum means selected three distinct patients (0.943, 0.866, and 0.531, respectively); these are frame selections, not patient-average scores. Extrema were chosen first, then the closest-median frame; exact ties were resolved by ascending pseudonymous patient ID, frame ID, side, and case ID. No diagnosis quota was imposed. Cyan solid outlines denote reference masks and orange dashed outlines denote accepted-component masks. Dice is 2TP/(2TP+FP+FN) on the full 768-by-768 rasters; rejected ROIs are represented by empty predictions and Dice=0. Only common black letterbox padding was removed, with identical contrast and scale. Displayed case labels are de-identified and contain no direct patient identifiers. These retrospective, outcome-selected examples are descriptive, not representative, and cannot estimate prevalence or comparative performance. A column's rank is across the four-model mean, not each model's own rank.

caption: Figure 4. Binary eye-level confusion matrices across five test splits.
note: Note. Each matrix presents eye-level predictions from the primary model-specific classifier. Cells show the arithmetic mean ± sample SD (ddof = 1) of within-seed true-row percentages for seeds 17, 42, 2026, 3407, and 9103. True rows include every intended eye, including abstentions, and sum to 100% before rounding. The colour scale is fixed at 0–100% for every panel. The diagonal reports failure-aware class recall (binary: specificity and sensitivity), agreeing with Table 3. These are descriptive summaries of overlapping holdouts, not pooled independent observations; SD is in percentage points.

caption: Figure 5. Direct three-class eye-level confusion matrices across five test splits.
note: Note. Each matrix presents eye-level predictions from the primary model-specific classifier. Cells show the arithmetic mean ± sample SD (ddof = 1) of within-seed true-row percentages for seeds 17, 42, 2026, 3407, and 9103. True rows include every intended eye, including abstentions, and sum to 100% before rounding. The colour scale is fixed at 0–100% for every panel. Diagonals report failure-aware eye-level class recall; aggregate eye-level outcomes are in Supplementary Table S24. Each seed includes 20 normal, 8 papilledema, and 8 pseudopapilledema eyes. Eyes within patients and overlapping seed holdouts are correlated; these summaries are descriptive, not pooled independent observations; SD is in percentage points.

caption: Supplementary Figure S1. Retrospective diagnosis-stratified segmentation and ROI coverage. Part 1 of 4.
note: Note. Exploratory diagnosis-stratified anatomical segmentation for YOLO26. Panels A–C show normal, papilledema and pseudopapilledema strata. Colored points show the five split-specific all-intended-frame Dice means and strict predicted-ROI coverage; transparent lines connect the two measurements from the same seed and do not denote a causal relationship. Black diamonds and whiskers show the arithmetic mean ± sample SD across five splits (not a confidence interval); values beneath each category repeat that summary. Each split includes 140 normal, 56 papilledema and 56 pseudopapilledema frames. Invalid predictions contribute zero Dice and remain in coverage denominators. One shared anatomical ROI was learned across diagnoses; these retrospective strata do not represent diagnosis-specific lesion segmentation. Test memberships overlap, so summaries are descriptive rather than independent-sample inference.

caption: Supplementary Figure S2. Descriptive raw-to-postprocessed segmentation changes. Part 1 of 4.
note: Note. Descriptive raw-versus-postprocessed anatomical segmentation for YOLO26. Panels A–C show Dice, IoU and HD95. Colored points are split-specific means, and transparent lines pair summaries from the same seed. Black diamonds and whiskers show mean ± sample SD across the five split means, not confidence intervals; values beneath each category repeat that summary. Dice and IoU retain all 252 intended frames per split, including invalid predictions scored as empty masks. HD95 is conditional on nonempty predictions and measured in pixels in the resized 768 × 768 analysis space. Test memberships overlap; this is descriptive boundary/overlap assessment, and no raw-versus-postprocessed hypothesis test was prespecified.

caption: Supplementary Figure S8. Binary eye-level failure-aware risk–coverage: YOLO26. Part 1 of 4.
note: Note. Five separate seed curves for the primary model-specific classifier use operational temperature-scaled eye probabilities. Each ranks all 36 intended eyes by descending absolute distance from the locked decision threshold; structural abstentions are appended at lowest confidence and counted as errors. Coverage is retained rank divided by 36, and risk is cumulative ordinary misclassification proportion, not 1 minus balanced accuracy. The terminal risk therefore equals 1 minus failure-aware accuracy. The saved AURC summary is the mean over all 36 rank risks. Curves are descriptive and do not establish a deployment rejection threshold, prospective safety or clinical benefit. Coordinates are supplied in data/binary_curve_coordinates.csv.

caption: Supplementary Figure S13. Three-class patient selective risk–coverage curves. Part 1 of 4.
note: Note. YOLO26 patient-level selective risk–coverage for the three-class task. Patients are ranked within seed by maximum calibrated class probability. Structural abstentions are appended at lowest confidence and count as errors; The horizontal coordinate is the included rank divided by all intended patients; after structural abstentions are appended, it is an accounting fraction rather than attainable prediction coverage.. Risk is the overall three-class error rate, not a class-specific error rate. All five seed traces remain separate; terminal risk equals one minus failure-aware accuracy.
